common_name: Swing Low Distylium (Prostrate Groundcover Evergreen Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to full shade; Swing Low's very low, ground-hugging habit makes it useful as a durable evergreen groundcover in spots too shaded for most flowering groundcovers.

directions: Swing Low is one of the lowest-growing distylium selections available, spreading wide while staying under 18 inches tall, which makes it a tough, evergreen alternative to traditional shade groundcovers like liriope or mondo grass in beds too shaded for turf. Its small, glossy, leathery leaves resist deer browsing and stay attractive year-round, with new growth tinged bronze-red before maturing to green, and inconspicuous small red flowers appear in late winter without significant ornamental impact. Like other distylium selections it is remarkably adaptable, tolerating wet or dry soil, heat, humidity, and both full sun and deep shade with minimal disease or pest pressure, and needs only an occasional trim to keep its spreading habit in bounds.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, strongly acidic soil in partial shade; Always Summer produces new flower flushes over a longer window than older gardenia cultivars, so regular feeding through the growing season supports the extended bloom.

directions: Always Summer is a reblooming gardenia bred to flower repeatedly from late spring well into fall rather than concentrating bloom into one or two flushes, giving a much longer season of the classic waxy white, intensely fragrant flowers than older gardenia cultivars provide. It holds a compact, rounded, well-branched habit with glossy dark-green foliage and, like other modern reblooming gardenias, benefits from regular feeding with an acid-forming fertilizer through the growing season to fuel the repeated flower flushes. Plant in humus-rich, consistently moist, strongly acidic soil in partial shade with protection from hot afternoon sun, and watch for the yellowing (chlorotic) foliage that signals insufficiently acidic soil, correcting with sulfur or an acidifying fertilizer as needed.

common_name: Plum Passion Nandina (Deep Plum-Red New Growth Heavenly Bamboo)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; new-growth color is most intense with several hours of direct sun, while afternoon shade helps prevent scorch in peak Gulf South summer heat.

directions: Plum Passion is a compact nandina selected for new foliage that emerges a deep plum-red to burgundy, maturing to green through the growing season before shifting back to purple-red tones in fall and winter cold, giving a longer window of rich color than many dwarf nandina cultivars that show red only in cool weather. Its dense, mounding habit fits foundation plantings and mixed borders without the tall, leggy cane growth of standard nandina, and like other modern dwarf selections it produces few or no berries, reducing the self-seeding that has made straight-species nandina invasive in parts of the Southeast. It needs little care beyond occasionally removing damaged canes to keep its naturally tidy shape.

common_name: Apple Blossom Camellia (Soft Pink-and-White Bicolor Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.5-6.5), humus-rich soil in partial shade; Apple Blossom is a classic, long-grown japonica selection valued for its delicate two-tone flowers on an easy-care, adaptable shrub.

directions: Apple Blossom is a long-cultivated camellia japonica prized for its semi-double flowers, which open a soft blush pink toward the petal edges fading to nearly white at the center, giving a delicate two-tone effect reminiscent of a spring apple blossom. It blooms in mid-to-late winter through early spring on a medium-sized, upright, well-branched evergreen shrub with the same glossy dark foliage typical of camellia japonica, providing color in the landscape during a season when little else is flowering. Grow in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, mulch to keep roots cool and moist, and prune lightly to shape only right after flowering, since next season's buds set over the following summer.
